a1.he: בְּאֶמְצַע יוֹבֵל, דְּכֹל כַּמָּה דְּלָא מָלְיָא לֵיהּ שָׁנָה לָא מְגָרַע לֵיהּ.

a2.he: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים עִם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ? הָא בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי: ״אֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים עִם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ!״ מָה טַעַם קָאָמַר: מָה טַעַם לֹא גּוֹאֲלִין לְאַחַר יוֹבֵל פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁנָה — מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים עִם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.

a3.he: אֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים עִם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֶּסֶף עַל פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרוֹת״ — שָׁנִים אַתָּה מְחַשֵּׁב, וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַשֵּׁב חֳדָשִׁים.

a4.he: מִנַּיִין שֶׁאִם אַתָּה רוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת חֳדָשִׁים לַשָּׁנָה עוֹשֶׂה? הֵיכִי דָּמֵי — כְּגוֹן דְּאַקְדְּשֵׁיהּ בְּפַלְגָא דְּאַרְבְּעִין וְתַמְנֵי.

a5.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן״, מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

a6.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַיּוֹבֵל, נוֹתֵן בְּזֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים ״חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף״. הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמוּקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, אוֹ סְלָעִים גְּבוֹהִים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — אֵינָן נִמְדָּדִין עִמָּהּ, פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן — נִמְדָּדִין עִמָּהּ.

a7.he: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל — נוֹתֵן סֶלַע וּפוּנְדְּיוֹן לְשָׁנָה, וְאִם אָמַר: ״הֲרֵינִי נוֹתֵן דְּבַר שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה״ — אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ, אֶלָּא נוֹתֵן אֶת כּוּלּוֹ כְּאֶחָד. אֶחָד בְּעָלִים וְאֶחָד כׇּל הָאָדָם, מָה בֵּין בְּעָלִים לְכׇל אָדָם? אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ, וְכׇל אָדָם אֵין נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ.

a8.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנָא: כּוֹר זֶרַע, וְלֹא כּוֹר תְּבוּאָה, מַפּוֹלֶת יָד, וְלֹא מַפּוֹלֶת שְׁוָורִים. תָּנֵי לֵוִי: לֹא מְעֻבֶּה וְלָא מֵידֵק, אֶלָּא בֵּינוֹנִי.

a9.he: הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמוּקִּים כּוּ׳. וְלִיקְדְּשׁוּ בְּאַנְפֵּי נַפְשַׁיְיהוּ!

a10.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָווּ בֵּית כּוֹר, לָא (הֲווֹ) קָדְשִׁי, וְהָתַנְיָא: שְׂדֵה, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ כָּעִנְיָן הַזֶּה, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת לֶתֶךְ וַחֲצִי לֶתֶךְ, סְאָה וְתַרְקַב וַחֲצִי תַרְקַב? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״שָׂדֶה״, מִכׇּל מָקוֹם!

a11.he: אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: הָכָא בִּנְקָעִים מְלֵאִים מַיִם, דְּלָאו בְּנֵי זְרִיעָה נִינְהוּ. דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי דּוּמְיָא דִסְלָעִים, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a12.he: אִי הָכִי, פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן נָמֵי! הָנְהוּ נְגָאנֵי דְאַרְעָא מִיקְּרוּ, שִׁידְרֵי דְּאַרְעָא מִיקְּרוּ.

a13.he: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן:

a14.he: ״וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ״, אַף מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ, שֶׁאִם אֲכָלָהּ הֶקְדֵּשׁ שָׁנָה אוֹ שְׁתַּיִם, אִי נָמֵי לֹא אֲכָלָהּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיְתָה לְפָנָיו — נוֹתֵן סֶלַע וּפוּנְדְּיוֹן לְשָׁנָה.

a15.he: וְאִם אָמַר ״הֲרֵינִי נוֹתֵן״ כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם אָמְרוּ בְּעָלִים ״הֲרֵינוּ נוֹתְנִין דְּבַר שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה״, שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לָהֶם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֶּסֶף״, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא כֶּסֶף כּוּלּוֹ כְּאֶחָד. אֶחָד בְּעָלִים וְאֶחָד כׇּל אָדָם, מָה בֵּין בְּעָלִים לְכׇל אָדָם? שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ, וְכׇל אָדָם אֵין נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ.

a16.he: מַתְנִי׳ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ וּגְאָלָהּ — אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה מִיָּדוֹ בַּיּוֹבֵל, גְּאָלָהּ בְּנוֹ — יוֹצְאָה לְאָבִיו בְּיוֹבֵל, גְּאָלָהּ אַחֵר אוֹ אֶחָד מֵהַקְּרוֹבִים, וּגְאָלָהּ מִיָּדוֹ — יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל.

a17.he: גְּאָלָהּ אֶחָד מִן הַכֹּהֲנִים, וַהֲרֵי הִיא תַּחַת יָדוֹ, לֹא יֹאמַר: הוֹאִיל וְהִיא יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל וַהֲרֵי הִיא תַּחַת יְדֵי — הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי, אֶלָּא יוֹצְאָה מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ וּמִתְחַלֶּקֶת לְכׇל אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים.

b2.he: ״אִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה״ — בְּעָלִים, ״וְאִם מָכַר אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה״ — גִּיזְבָּר.

b3.he: ״לְאִישׁ אַחֵר״ — לְאַחֵר, וְלֹא לַבֵּן. אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: לְאַחֵר וְלֹא לַבֵּן, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְאַחֵר וְלֹא לָאָח? כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אִישׁ״ — הֲרֵי אָח אָמוּר, הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״אַחֵר״ — וְלֹא לַבֵּן.

b4.he: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַבֵּן וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת הָאָח? מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי הַבֵּן, שֶׁכֵּן קָם תַּחַת אָבִיו לִיעִידָה וּלְעֶבֶד עִבְרִי.

b5.he: אַדְּרַבָּה, מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי אֶת הָאָח, שֶׁכֵּן קָם תַּחַת אָחִיו לְיִיבּוּם. כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יִבּוּם אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בֵּן? הָא יֵשׁ בֵּן — אֵין יִבּוּם.

b6.he: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ, דְּהָכָא תַּרְתֵּי, וְהָכָא חֲדָא!

b7.he: מִשּׁוּם דְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי מֵהַאי פִּירְכָא נָמֵי הוּא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ יִבּוּם אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בֵּן?

b8.he: בָּעֵי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: בַּת מַהוּ שֶׁתַּעֲמִיד שָׂדֶה לְאָבִיהָ? כֵּיוָן דִּלְעִנְיַן יִבּוּם, בֵּן וּבַת כִּי הֲדָדֵי פָּטְרִי — מוֹקְמָה, אוֹ דִילְמָא כֵּיוָן דִּלְעִנְיַן נַחֲלָה, בַּת בִּמְקוֹם בֵּן כִּי אַחֵר דָּמְיָא — לָא מוֹקְמָה.

b9.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא אַחֵר בִּמְקוֹם בֵּן, וְהָא נָמֵי בִּמְקוֹם בֵּן כִּי אַחֵר דָּמְיָא.

b10.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: אִשָּׁה מִי מַעֲמִיד לָהּ שָׂדֶה? בַּעַל מוֹקֵים לַהּ, שֶׁכֵּן יוֹרְשָׁהּ, אוֹ דִילְמָא בֵּן מוֹקֵים לַהּ, שֶׁכֵּן נוֹטֵל בָּרָאוּי כְּבַמּוּחְזָק? תֵּיקוּ.

b11.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל, מַהוּ שֶׁתֵּצֵא לַכֹּהֲנִים?

b12.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ? ״וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ... וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל״ — דְּבַת גֵּירָעוֹן — אִין, דְּלָאו בַּת גֵּירָעוֹן — לָא.

b13.he: אַדְּרַבָּה, ״אִם לֹא יִגְאַל הַשָּׂדֶה... וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל״, וְהַאי נָמֵי בַּת גְּאוּלָּה הִיא.

b14.he: גְּאָלָהּ אֶחָד מִן הַכֹּהֲנִים כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר?

b15.he: מִנַּיִן לְשָׂדֶה שֶׁיּוֹצָא לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל, וּגְאָלָהּ אֶחָד מִן הַכֹּהֲנִים, מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר: ״הוֹאִיל וְיוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֵן, הֲרֵי תַּחַת יָדִי, וּתְהֵא שֶׁלִּי?״ וְדִין הוּא: בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים אֲנִי זוֹכֶה, בְּשֶׁל עַצְמִי לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

b16.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״, אֲחוּזָּה שֶׁלּוֹ, וְאֵין זֶה שֶׁלּוֹ. הָא כֵּיצַד? יוֹצָא מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ וּמִתְחַלֶּקֶת לְאֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים.

b17.he: מַתְנִי׳ הִגִּיעַ יוֹבֵל וְלֹא נִגְאֲלָה, הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין לְתוֹכָהּ וְנוֹתְנִין אֶת דָּמֶיהָ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: נִכְנָסִין וְלֹא נוֹתְנִין.

b18.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא נִכְנָסִין וְלֹא נוֹתְנִין, אֶלָּא נִקְרֵאת ״שְׂדֵה רְטוּשִׁין״ עַד הַיּוֹבֵל הַשֵּׁנִי. הִגִּיעַ הַיּוֹבֵל הַשֵּׁנִי וְלֹא נִגְאֲלָה, נִקְרֵאת ״רְטוּשֵׁי רְטוּשִׁין״ עַד הַיּוֹבֵל הַשְּׁלִישִׁי. לְעוֹלָם אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין לְתוֹכָהּ עַד שֶׁיִּגְאָלֶנָּה אַחֵר.

b19.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? גָּמַר ״קֹדֶשׁ״ ״קֹדֶשׁ״ מִמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת,

b20.he: מָה לְהַלָּן בְּדָמִים — אַף כָּאן בְּדָמִים.

b21.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, גָּמַר ״קֹדֶשׁ״ ״קֹדֶשׁ״ מִכִּבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת, מָה לְהַלָּן בְּחִנָּם, אַף כָּאן בְּחִנָּם.

b22.he: וְרַבִּי [יְהוּדָה] נָמֵי נֵילַיף מִכִּבְשֵׂי עֲצֶרֶת! דָּנִין קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת

messages.text: Continued from 24b: the mishna said one may not redeem an ancestral field “less than a year after the Jubilee.” According to Rav, who holds that a field may be consecrated in the Jubilee Year itself, the Gemara asked what “after the Jubilee” refers to.
It is referring to any year in the middle of the Jubilee cycle.

notes.he: כלומר האי אחר אפי' אחר עשרים או שלשים שנה קאי ומאי פחות שנה דקאמר הכי קאמר הבא לגאול באמצע יובל וליתן סלע ופונדיון לשנים הבאים והיה עומד בניסן שהוא אמצע שנה לא יאמר חצי סלע וחצי פונדיון אני נותן משנה זו אלא נותן סלע ופונדיון שלם והיינו דקאמר אין גואלין בפחות משנה דכמה דלא נפקא לה כולה שתא לא מיגרע ליה כלל ולא יהיב גאולת חצי שנה אלא גאולת שנה שלימה:
notes.en: In the middle of the Jubilee: that is, this “after” [the Jubilee] stands even after twenty or thirty years. And what is the “less than a year” that it says? This is what it means: one who comes to redeem in the middle of the Jubilee [cycle], to give a sela and a pundeyon for the coming years, and he was standing in Nisan, which is the middle of the year, may not say: I give half a sela and half a pundeyon for this year; rather, he gives a whole sela and pundeyon. And this is what it says: one does not redeem for less than a year, for as long as the whole year has not gone out, nothing is deducted for it at all, and he does not give the redemption of half a year but the redemption of a full year.

messages.text: The mishna’s statement should be read as follows: After the Jubilee Year, one may not redeem a field for less than the price of a year, meaning that as long as a year has not been completed, he does not deduct it from the price of redemption.

notes.dh: דכמה דלא מליא ליה שנה לא מגרעא ליה
notes.he: כלומר שאם היתה ביד הקדש ה' שנים ומחצה ובא לגואלה לא יאמר אותן ה' שנים ומחצה שהיתה ביד הקדש איגרע כנגדו ו' שקלים ושש פונדיונין ואחשוב אותה חצי שנה כאילו היתה שלימה אלא יחשבנה עם השנים הנותרות עד היובל ליתן סלע ופונדיון לשנה להקדש בשבילה:
notes.en: As long as the year is not complete, nothing is deducted for it: that is, if it was in the possession of the Temple five and a half years and he comes to redeem it, he may not say: for those five and a half years that it was in the possession of the Temple I will deduct six shekels and six pundeyon against it, counting the half year as if it were complete. Rather, he counts it with the years remaining until the Jubilee, to give the Temple a sela and a pundeyon a year for it.

messages.text: For example, if there are five and a half years remaining until the Jubilee Year, he must give six sela and six pundeyon for its redemption, not five and a half of each of a sela and a pundeyon.

What is the tanna teaching us? Is he saying that one does not count months in order to lower the price to be paid to the Temple treasury? Such an interpretation is untenable, as that halakha is taught explicitly in the following line of the mishna: One does not count months in order to lower the price to be paid to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: כדאמרן שאם בא לגאלה חמש שנים וחצי לפני היובל אין מחשבין אותן ששה חדשים שיצאו משנה לשנה ששית אלא נותן ששה סלעים וששה פונדיונין]:
notes.en: [That one does not count months with the Temple: as we said, that if he comes to redeem it five and a half years before the Jubilee, one does not count for him those six months that have gone out of the year into the sixth year; rather, he gives six sela and six pundeyon.]

notes.dh: מאי קמ"ל דאין מחשבין חדשים עם ההקדש
notes.he: כלומר דאם הקדישה ובחצי שנה גאלה לא יגרע כנגדו להקדש חצי סלע וחצי פונדיון:
notes.en: What is he teaching us, that one does not count months with the Temple? That is, that if he consecrated it and redeemed it after half a year, he does not deduct against the Temple for it half a sela and half a pundeyon.

notes.he: לה דאין מחשבין כלל:
notes.en: But it is taught explicitly: that one does not count [months] at all.

messages.text: The tanna is not attempting to teach a separate halakha here. Rather, he employs the style known as: What is the reason, and the mishna is to be read as follows: What is the reason that one may not redeem a field after the Jubilee Year with less than the price of a complete year? It is because one does not count months in order to lower the price to be paid to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: אמר לך רב אין חדא מילתא היא ומה טעם קאמר הילכך מיהא ליכא למידק למעוטי שנת היובל עצמה:
notes.en: Rav will tell you: yes, it is one matter, and it is stating “what is the reason.” Therefore, at any rate, there is no inference to be drawn to exclude the Jubilee Year itself.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: One does not count months in order to lower the price to be paid to the Temple treasury, but the Temple treasury may count months in order to raise the price of redemption.

From where is it derived that one does not count months in order to lower the price to be paid to the Temple treasury? The verse states: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the money according to the years that remain until the Jubilee Year, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation.” This teaches that you are to calculate years, but you are not to count months.
messages.lead: With regard to this statement, the Sages taught in a baraita:

verse.he: וְאִם־אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף עַל־פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if the land is consecrated after the jubilee, the priest shall compute the price according to the years that are left until the jubilee year, and its assessment shall be so reduced;

notes.he: כל מה שנותר חשוב שנים:
notes.en: The years that remain: whatever remains counts as years.

messages.text: Furthermore, from where is it derived that if you, i.e., the priest representing the Temple treasury, want to consider months as a year so that it will be considered as though a complete year has passed, you may do so?

notes.he: לחשוב אותן חדשים שיצאו כאילו הן שנה והוי רווחא דידיה:
notes.en: To make months a year: to count those months that have gone out as if they were a year, and that is its [the Temple’s] gain.

messages.text: And what are the circumstances in which the priest would want to do this? For example, in a case where one consecrated the field in the middle of the forty-eighth year and wishes to redeem it.

notes.he: דאי חשבת לחדשים שיצאו ביציאה גמורה הוו להו פחות משתי שנים ואינה נגאלת בגירוע:
notes.en: And what are the circumstances? Where he consecrated it in the middle of the forty-eighth [year]: for if you count the months that have gone out as fully gone out, there are less than two years [left], and it is not redeemed with a deduction.

notes.he: לאו דוקא נקט דאקדשיה דלא בהקדש תליא מילתא כי אם בגאולה:
notes.en: Where he consecrated it in the middle of the forty-eighth: “consecrated” is not meant precisely, for the matter does not depend on the consecration but only on the redemption.

messages.text: In such a case, if the months that have passed are calculated as a complete year, then the halakha with regard to the redemption of a field in the year preceding the Jubilee Year is in effect, and the field must be redeemed according to its full valuation of fifty sela per beit kor, rather than the redemption price of two sela and two pundeyon per beit kor that would apply if the calculation were based on two years remaining until the Jubilee.

notes.he: שלא יחשוב עם ההקדש בחצי שנה או בח' חדשים כמו שהקדישה בסוף שנה לפחות כנגדם (למקדש) [להקד'] סלע ופונדיון או כנגד החדשים שעברו כדקתני בברייתא. שנים שלימות שלא היתה (ברשותו) [ברשות הקדש] אתה מחשב לפחות כנגדן סלע ופונדיון ולא כנגד חדשים אבל הקדש מחשב חדשים שנה כדמפרש בגמרא כגון דאקדשה בפלגא דארבעין ותמני דסד"א האי דאמרינן דאין מקדישין לגאול בגירוע פחות מב' שנים לפני היובל הני מילי כי אקדשה בסוף מ"ח אבל כי אקדשה בחצי מ"ח לימא דליהוי כמי שהקדישה בתחילת מ"ח דהוו ב' שנים לפני היובל ולגאל בגירוע קמ"ל דעבדינן הני חדשים שנה כאילו הקדישה בסוף מ"ח משום רווחא דהקדש דאינו גואל בגירוע אלא נותן נ' שקל להקדש והיינו אבל הקדש מחשב חדשים שנה וכן נמי אם עמדה ברשות הקדש עשר שנים ומחצה לא יחשוב המקדיש אלא עשר שנים ואותה חצי שנה יחשבנה בשנה שלימה עם השנים הנותרות ויתן בעד אותה חצי שנה נמי סלע ופונדיון כשנה שלימה עם השנים הנותרות עד היובל:
notes.en: One does not count months for the Temple: he may not count against the Temple for half a year or eight months, as if he had consecrated it at the end of the year, to reduce a sela and a pundeyon against them, or against the months that passed, as is taught in the baraita. Complete years in which it was not [in the Temple’s possession] you count, to reduce a sela and a pundeyon against them, but not against months. But the Temple counts months as a year, as is explained in the Gemara: for example, where he consecrated it in the middle of the forty-eighth. For it might enter your mind: what we say, that one does not consecrate [so as] to redeem with a deduction less than two years before the Jubilee, applies when he consecrated it at the end of the forty-eighth; but when he consecrated it in the middle of the forty-eighth, let us say it is as though he consecrated it at the beginning of the forty-eighth, which is two years before the Jubilee, and it is redeemed with a deduction. It teaches us that we make these months a year, as though he consecrated it at the end of the forty-eighth, for the Temple’s gain, so that he does not redeem with a deduction but gives fifty shekels to the Temple; and this is “but the Temple counts months as a year.” And likewise, if it stood in the Temple’s possession ten and a half years, the one who consecrated it counts only ten years, and that half year he counts as a full year with the remaining years, and for that half year too he gives a sela and a pundeyon, like a full year, with the years remaining until the Jubilee.

messages.text: From where is this halakha derived? The verse states: “Then the priest shall reckon for him,” which indicates that the priest reckons for him in any case, i.e., the calculation is to be performed according to his discretion.

verse.he: וְאִם־אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף עַל־פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if the land is consecrated after the jubilee, the priest shall compute the price according to the years that are left until the jubilee year, and its assessment shall be so reduced;

notes.he: שיחשוב (מ"מ כדי) שיהא ריוח להקדש:
notes.en: The verse states: “Then the priest shall reckon for him,” in any case: that he reckons so that there is gain for the Temple.

messages.caption: Counting the years of a field’s redemption: months never lower the price, but the priest may count months as a year in the Temple’s favor, with the mishna’s rates below.

messages.text: Mishna

In the case of one who consecrates his ancestral field during a period when the Jubilee Year is observed and wishes to redeem it, he gives the Temple treasury fifty sela, a talmudic measure referred to in the Bible as silver shekels, for an area required for sowing a ḥomer, a measure known in talmudic terminology as one kor, of barley seed (see Leviticus 27:16).

notes.he: בזמן שהיובל נוהג אבל בזמן שאין היובל נוהג פודה אותה בשוויה כשאר הקדישות:
notes.en: Mishna. At the time of the Jubilee: when the Jubilee is in force. But when the Jubilee is not in force, one redeems it at its value, like other consecrated property.

notes.he: בזמן שהיובל נוהג:
notes.en: At the time of the Jubilee: when the Jubilee is in force.

notes.he: לאלתר לאחר היובל כשהוא גואלה מיד [ההקדש] נותן [בזרע] חומר שעורים נ' שקל:
notes.en: He gives: right after the Jubilee, when he redeems it from [the Temple], he gives fifty shekels [for the sowing of] a ḥomer of barley.

messages.text: If there were crevices [neka’im] ten handbreadths deep in the field, or if there were boulders ten handbreadths high, then when calculating the redemption price those areas are not measured with the rest of the field. But if the depth of the crevices, or the height of the boulders, was less than that amount, they are measured with the rest of the field.

notes.he: והן נפדין בשווין והשאר לפי חשבון חמשים סלעים לבית כור:
notes.en: They are not measured with it: and they are redeemed at their value, and the rest according to the reckoning of fifty sela per beit kor.

notes.he: מפני שהן רשות לעצמן:
notes.en: They are not measured with it: because they are a domain of their own.

messages.text: If he consecrated the field two or three years before the Jubilee Year and wishes to redeem it, he gives the Temple treasury a sela and a pundeyon, a pundeyon being one forty-eighth of a sela, per year remaining until the Jubilee Year.
And if he said: I will give the payment for each year during that year, one does not listen to him; rather, he must give the entire sum in one payment.

This is the halakha both with regard to a case where the owner redeems the field and a case where any other person redeems the field. What then is the difference between redemption by the owner and redemption by any other person? It is only that the owner gives an extra one-fifth in addition to the payment, and any other person who redeems the field does not give the additional one-fifth.

notes.he: פודה בית חומר בחמשים שקל בין שהיא שוה אלף שקלים בין שאינה שוה אלא ה' שקלים:
notes.en: And any person: redeems a beit ḥomer for fifty shekels, whether it is worth a thousand shekels or worth only five shekels.

notes.he: דכתיב ואם גאל יגאל את השדה המקדיש אותו וגו':
notes.en: That the owner gives a fifth: as it is written: “And if he that sanctified the field will indeed redeem it” and so on [“then he shall add the fifth part of the money,” Leviticus 27:19].

messages.text: Gemara

The phrase: “The sowing of a ḥomer of barley shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver,” is referring to an area required for sowing one kor, thirty se’a, of barley seed, and not an area that yields one kor of barley crop, which is significantly smaller.

verse.he: וְאִם ׀ מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ לְפִי זַרְעוֹ זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף׃
verse.en: If anyone consecrates to GOD a land-holding, its assessment shall be in accordance with its seed requirement: fifty shekels of silver to a ḥomer of barley seed.

notes.he: שיכולין לזרוע בו כור:
notes.en: Gemara. A kor of seed: in which one can sow a kor.

notes.he: קרקע שקוצרין הימנו כור תבואה דהוי בציר מכור זרע טובא דבההוא לא בעי חמשים אלא לפי חשבון הזרע או שליש כור או רביע כור:
notes.en: And not a kor of crop: ground from which one reaps a kor of crop, which is much smaller than a kor of seed; for that one does not require fifty, but according to the reckoning of the seed, a third of a kor or a quarter of a kor.

notes.he: כלומר כשהוא מודד כמה כור יש בו מודד במקום שראוי לזרוע בו כור דהיינו יותר ממקום שיכול ליגדל בו כור תבואה לפי שגרגיר זרע יעשה שיבולת תבואה והיינו ריוח של מקדיש דאי אזיל בתר כור תבואה היה נותן הרבה שקלים אלא בתר כור זרע אזיל:
notes.en: A kor of seed and not a kor of crop: that is, when he measures how many kor are in it, he measures by the area fit to sow a kor in it, which is more than an area in which a kor of crop can grow, since a grain of seed makes an ear of grain. And this is the gain of the one who consecrated it, for if it went by a kor of crop he would give many shekels; rather, it goes by a kor of seed.

messages.text: This area is measured according to a field sowed by hand and not sowed by oxen. Since oxen sow the field by pulling a planter, which spreads the seeds at a higher density, the area containing one kor sown by oxen is smaller than the area of one kor sown by hand.

notes.he: שזורעין ביד:
notes.en: The falling of the hand: that one sows by hand.

notes.he: שהיו רגילין לתת שקין מלאין זרע על השוורים ומנוקבין השקין מתחתיהן נקבין רחבים ומוליכין אותן ע"פ המחרישה והזרע נופל וגדולה קרקע המקבלת כור זרע במפולת יד שאינו עבה מקרקע המקבלת כור זרע במפולת זרע שוורים שהיא עבה:
notes.en: And not the falling of oxen: they used to put sacks full of seed on the oxen, the sacks pierced underneath with wide holes, and lead them along the plow, and the seed falls. And ground that takes a kor of seed sown by the falling of the hand, which is not dense, is larger than ground that takes a kor of seed sown by the falling of oxen, which is dense.

notes.he: זרוע במפולת יד ולא זרוע במפולת שוורים [דהכי הוו זרעי במפולת שוורים] היו ממלאין שק [מלא דגן] והיו מניחין אותו ע"ג העגלה על הקנקן ובקנקן היה נקב והיה מושך העגלה ע"ג התלם והיה נופל הדגן דרך אותו נקב וכך היו זורעין בשוורים ועכשיו מי שזורע במפולת יד מפוזר יותר הזרע ותופש בית כור זרע במפולת יד מקום מרובה בשדה יותר מבמפולת שוורים לפי שאינו זורע בשוה אלא פעמים נופל הרבה ביחד מן הנקב ופעמים נופל מן הזרע מועט:
notes.en: A kor of seed: sown by the falling of the hand and not sown by the falling of oxen. [For this is how they sowed by the falling of oxen:] they would fill a sack [full of grain] and set it on the cart over the container, and in the container there was a hole; the cart would be drawn along the furrow and the grain would fall through that hole, and so they sowed with oxen. Now one who sows by hand scatters the seed more, and a beit kor of seed sown by hand takes up a larger area of the field than by oxen, because it [sowing by oxen] does not sow evenly: sometimes much falls together from the hole and sometimes little of the seed falls.

messages.text: The area is not measured according to the sowing of a particularly dense layer of seeds, nor a sparse layer, but rather in accordance with an average amount of seeds.

notes.he: אין משערין בזרע מעובה שהוא הפסידו של פודה:
notes.en: It is taught: one does not measure by densely sown seed, which is the loss of the one who redeems;

notes.he: בזרע מידק שהוא הפסד דהקדש דהוי בית כור גדול אלא בזריעה בינונית:
notes.en: Nor: by sparse seed, which is a loss to the Temple, since that would be a large beit kor; but by average sowing.

notes.he: מעובה שנותנין בה זרע מרובה. מידק שנותנין זרע מועט ובלע"ז קליי"ר:
notes.en: Dense: where much seed is put in. Sparse: where little seed is put in. (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.)

notes.he: מפולת יד שאמרו:
notes.en: Levi taught: [about] the falling of the hand that they spoke of.

notes.he: שמפילין הרבה ביחד דהיינו פסידא דמקדיש שירבו הכורים:
notes.en: Not dense: where much is dropped together, which is the loss of the one who consecrated it, since the kors would multiply.

notes.he: שמפזר יותר מדאי שזה הפסד של הקדש שממעט בכורים אלא בינונים:
notes.en: Nor sparse: where he scatters too widely, which is a loss to the Temple, since it reduces the kors; rather, average.

messages.text: And let them be consecrated by themselves, as they are fit for sowing, and therefore they should require redemption at the same rate as the rest of the field. Accordingly, one could simply measure the field together with the crevices, and the measurement will be equal to the sum total of the sizes of the field and any crevices.
messages.quote: there were crevices ten handbreadths deep in the field … are not measured with the rest of the field

notes.he: הנך נקעים באנפי נפשייהו וליפרקו נמי לפי חשבון חמשים לבית כור ומה הנאה יש במה שאין נמדדים עמה הא אינהו נמי הכי מיפרקי:
notes.en: And let them be consecrated: these crevices by themselves, and let them also be redeemed according to the reckoning of fifty per beit kor. And what benefit is there in their not being measured with it? They too are redeemed in just this way!

notes.he: פירשתי בב"ב (דף קג.) וקדושין (דף סא.):
notes.en: And let them be consecrated by themselves: I have explained this in Bava Batra (103a) and Kiddushin (61a).

messages.text: And if you would say that the mishna is referring to crevices that together take up only a small area, and since they do not measure a beit kor they are not consecrated, that cannot be correct: But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

The verse states: “And if a man shall sanctify for the Lord part of his ancestral field.” Why must the verse state: “Field”? Since it is stated in the same verse: “Your valuation shall be according to its sowing; the sowing of a ḥomer of barley shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver,” one might say: I have derived only that this is the halakha when he consecrated a field like this, i.e., one measuring at least a beit kor.

verse.he: וְאִם ׀ מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ לְפִי זַרְעוֹ זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף׃
verse.en: If anyone consecrates to GOD a land-holding, its assessment shall be in accordance with its seed requirement: fifty shekels of silver to a ḥomer of barley seed.

notes.he: ה"ל למיכתב ואם מאחוזתו יקדיש איש וגו':
notes.en: “Field”, why must the verse state it? It could have written: “And if a man shall sanctify part of his ancestral possession,” and so on.

notes.he: בית כור שלם:
notes.en: In this manner: a full beit kor.

notes.he: לכתוב ואם מאחוזתו יקדיש:
notes.en: “Field”, why must the verse state it? [It could have] written: “And if of his ancestral possession he shall sanctify.”

notes.he: בשיעור הזה זרע חומר שעורים בחמשים:
notes.en: In this manner: in this measure, the sowing of a ḥomer of barley for fifty.

messages.text: From where is it derived to include fields that are fit for sowing only a half-kor or half of a half-kor, a se’a or a half-se’a [vetarkav], or even half of a half-se’a? The verse states: “Field,” indicating that one may consecrate a field in any case, regardless of size.

notes.he: חצי כור:
notes.en: Letekh: half a kor.

notes.he: חצי סאה תרי וקב דהיינו שלש קבין שהן חצי סאה:
notes.en: Tarkav: half a se’a; “two and a kav” [tarei-kav], that is, three kav, which are half a se’a.

notes.he: אם הקדיש שדה לתך וחצי לתך שצריך לפדות:
notes.en: From where: if he consecrated a field of a letekh or half a letekh, that he must redeem it.

notes.he: דקדשה:
notes.en: The verse states “field”, in any case: that it is consecrated.

messages.text: Here, the mishna is referring to crevices that are full of water, which are not fit for sowing. Accordingly, they are not measured with the field, as the verse states that the valuation is in accordance with the areas fit for sowing barley seeds.

The language is also precise, as the tanna teaches the halakha with regard to crevices similar to the way he teaches that of boulders, which are also not fit for sowing, as it states: If there were crevices ten handbreadths deep or boulders ten handbreadths high. Conclude from this that the mishna is referring to crevices unfit for sowing.

notes.he: דלאו בני זריעה [נינהו]:
notes.en: Similar to boulders: which are not fit for sowing.

messages.text: If so, then when the difference in height between the field and the crevices or boulders is less than ten handbreadths, they should also not be measured with the field. Why does the mishna indicate that they are measured with the field in this case?

notes.he: כיון דאוקימתא דמליאין מים פחות מיכן נמי אמאי נמדדין עמה:
notes.en: If so: since we have interpreted it as crevices full of water, why are those less than this measured with it?

messages.text: These crevices less than ten handbreadths deep are called cracks of the ground, and these boulders less than ten handbreadths tall are called spines of the ground. As there is no great disparity in surface level between them and the field itself, they are deemed part of the field and are therefore measured with it, despite the fact that they are unfit for sowing.

notes.he: נקעים פחותין מי'. נגאני דארעא ספלים של קרקע שהמים מתכנסין שם ועל שם הקרקע הם נקראים ואינן חשובין בפני עצמן. וסלעים הנמוכין מעשרה שדרי דארעא מיקרו כמו שדרה של בהמה שגבוהה:
notes.en: Negani: crevices less than ten [handbreadths]. Negani de’ara are basins of the ground where the water gathers; they are named after the ground and are not considered by themselves. And boulders lower than ten are called spines of the ground, like the spine of an animal, which is raised.

notes.he: ספלים של שדה שמשימין בהן מים כדי להשקותה ונחשבין כשדה וכן נמי סלעים פחותין מי' [שפנד"ש בלע"ז] שדרי דארעא מיקרו. שכך נמצאין הרבה בשדות ונחשבין כשדה:
notes.en: Because they are called cracks of the ground: basins of the field in which water is placed to irrigate it, and they are considered as field. And likewise boulders less than ten [(an Old French gloss)] are called spines of the ground, for many such are found in fields, and they are considered as field.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that if he consecrated the field two or three years before the Jubilee Year and wishes to redeem it, he gives the Temple treasury a sela and a pundeyon per year. In this regard, the Sages taught a baraita that deals with the verse: “But if he sanctifies his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall reckon for him the money according to the years that remain until the Jubilee Year, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation.”
messages.quote: he consecrated the field two or three years before the Jubilee

verse.he: וְאִם־אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף עַל־פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if the land is consecrated after the jubilee, the priest shall compute the price according to the years that are left until the jubilee year, and its assessment shall be so reduced;

messages.text: The apparently superfluous phrase “And a deduction shall be made from your valuation” teaches that even the years that passed from the consecration of the field are deducted, and not only the years that passed before it was consecrated.

notes.he: דכי היכי דמיגרעא באותן שנים שעמדה בידו שלא הקדישה ה"נ מיגרעא מחמת אותן שנים שעמדה ביד הקדש משעת הקדש עד שעת פדיון:
notes.en: Even from the consecration: just as it is deducted for those years in which it stood in his possession when he had not consecrated it, so too it is deducted for those years in which it stood in the possession of the Temple, from the time of consecration until the time of redemption.

messages.text: That is, if the Temple treasury benefited from the field’s produce for a year or two, or if the Temple treasury did not benefit from it but the field nevertheless remained before it, i.e., in the possession of the Temple treasury, he gives a sela and a pundeyon for each remaining year until the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: שלא זרע בה גזבר כלום ולא השכירה לשום אדם שהיתה לפניו ביד הקדש מנכה סלע ופונדיון לכל שנה ושנה מיובל שעבר עד שעת פדיון:
notes.en: Or even if it did not consume it: the treasurer did not sow anything in it and did not rent it out to anyone, but it was before him in the possession of the Temple; he deducts a sela and a pundeyon for each and every year from the Jubilee that passed until the time of redemption.

notes.he: כלומר שכשם [שאם הקדישה עשר שנים לאחר היובל וגאלה לסוף עשרים שמנכה לו] אותן שנים שהיתה ברשות בעלים שאינו נותן מהם סלע ופונדיון כך אם אכלה הקדש שנה או שתים [או י'] מנכה לו סלע ופונדיון לכל אותן שנים שהיתה ברשות הקדש ואינו נותן סלע ופונדיון אלא מן השנים של אחר הפדיון תוך היובל:
notes.en: “And a deduction shall be made from your valuation,” even from the consecration: that is, just as [if he consecrated it ten years after the Jubilee and redeemed it at the end of twenty, they deduct for him] those years that it was in the owner’s possession, for which he does not give a sela and a pundeyon, so if the Temple consumed it a year or two [or ten], they deduct for him a sela and a pundeyon for all those years that it was in the Temple’s possession, and he gives a sela and a pundeyon only for the years after the redemption within the Jubilee [cycle].

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: And if he said: I will give the payment for each year during that year, one does not listen to him; rather, he must give the entire sum in one payment.
messages.quote: And if he said: I will give the payment for each year during that year

messages.text: From where is it derived that if the owner said: I will give the payment for each year during that year, that one does not listen to him? The verse states: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the money.” The term “the money” indicates that the priest does not reckon the price for him unless all of the money will be paid together as one sum.

verse.he: וְאִם־אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף עַל־פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if the land is consecrated after the jubilee, the priest shall compute the price according to the years that are left until the jubilee year, and its assessment shall be so reduced;

notes.dh: ואם אמר הריני נותן דבר שנה בשנה
notes.he: בכל שנה סלע ופונדיון אין שומעין לו [שנאמר וחשב לו הכהן את הכסף כמה מגיע לו ליתן עד היובל ויתנו ביחד]:
notes.en: And if he said: I will give for each year during the year: a sela and a pundeyon each year, one does not listen to him [as it is said: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the money,” how much it comes to for him to give until the Jubilee, and they give it together].

messages.text: This is the halakha with regard to both the owner and any other person. What then is the difference between redemption by the owner and redemption by any other person? It is that the owner gives an extra one-fifth in addition to the payment, and any other person does not give the additional one-fifth.

notes.he: רשאין לפדות זרע חומר שעורים בנ' שקל:
notes.en: Both the owner and any person: may redeem the sowing of a ḥomer of barley for fifty shekels.

notes.he: מוסיפין על נ' שקל חומש שנא' ואם גאל יגאל את השדה המקדיש אותו ויסף חמישית כסף:
notes.en: Only that the owner: adds a fifth on top of the fifty shekels, as it is said: “And if he that sanctified the field will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of the money” (Leviticus 27:19).

messages.text: Mishna
If one consecrated his ancestral field and then redeemed it himself, it is not removed from his possession to be divided among the priests during the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: להיות מתחלקת לכהנים כי היכי דהוה אי פריק לה איניש אחרינא דהוה נפקא ביובל מתחלקת לכהנים כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״א) והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל וגו':
notes.en: Mishna. It does not leave his possession in the Jubilee: to be divided among the priests, as it would if another person had redeemed it, when it would leave in the Jubilee to be divided among the priests, as it is written: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” and so on (Leviticus 27:21).

messages.text: If his son redeemed it, the field is removed from the son’s possession and returns to his father during the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: ולא לכהנים כדיליף בברייתא בגמ':
notes.en: His son redeemed it, it goes out to his father in the Jubilee: and not to the priests, as is derived in the baraita in the Gemara.

notes.he: במקומו:
notes.en: His son redeemed it: in his place.

notes.he: ואינה יוצאה לכהנים (ואינו בא לההוא עצמו):
notes.en: It goes out to his father in the Jubilee: and does not go out to the priests. [A printer’s note suggests reading: and it is as though he himself redeemed it.] (And it does not come to that one himself [the son].)

messages.text: But if another person or one of his other relatives redeemed the field and the owner subsequently redeemed it from his possession, the field is removed from the owner’s possession and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: מיד גזבר ובא המקדיש וגאלה מיד קרובו יוצאה ביובל ומתחלקת לכהנים כי היכי דהוה נפיק מידיה דההוא קרוב דאתי האי מחמתיה:
notes.en: One of his relatives redeemed it: from the treasurer, and the one who consecrated it came and redeemed it from his relative’s possession: it goes out in the Jubilee and is divided among the priests, just as it would have gone out of that relative’s possession, since this one came [to hold it] through him.

notes.dh: גאלה אחר או אחד מן הקרובים
notes.he: וחזר זה המקדיש וגאלה מידו (אינה) יוצאה מידו ביובל:
notes.en: Another or one of the relatives redeemed it: and this one who consecrated it went back and redeemed it from his possession, it goes out of his possession in the Jubilee. [The printed text has “does not” before “go out” in parentheses, marking it as an error.]

messages.text: If one of the priests redeemed the field and when the Jubilee arrived it was in his possession, he may not say: Since it is removed from the possession of the one who redeemed it and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, and since it is already in my possession, it is mine. Rather, the field is removed from his possession and is divided among all his brethren, the priests.

notes.he: מיד גזבר לא יאמר הואיל ואם גאלה ישראל היתה יוצאה לי ולחביריי ביובל ועכשיו שהרי היא תחת ידי שגאלתיה אין לך כהן גדול ממני ותהא שלי:
notes.en: A priest redeemed it: from the treasurer. He may not say: Since, had an Israelite redeemed it, it would go out to me and my fellows in the Jubilee, and now it is in my possession, for I redeemed it, there is no priest with a greater claim than I, so let it be mine.

notes.dh: לא גאלה המקדיש וגאלה אחד מן הכהנים
notes.he: והרי היא תחת ידו ביובל. לא יאמר כו':
notes.en: The one who consecrated it did not redeem it, and one of the priests redeemed it, and it is in his possession at the Jubilee: he may not say, and so on.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that if one consecrated his ancestral field and his son redeemed it from the Temple treasury, the field returns to the original owner when the Jubilee arrives. By contrast, if another person redeemed it, the field is transferred to the priests during the Jubilee Year. With regard to this matter, the Sages taught a baraita analyzing the verse: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore. But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord, as a dedicated field; his ancestral possession shall be for the priest.”
messages.quote: If his son redeemed it … to his father during the Jubilee

verse.he: וְאִם־לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה וְאִם־מָכַר אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד׃ וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: But if the one [who consecrated it] did not redeem the land, and the land was sold to another party, it shall no longer be redeemable: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

messages.text: The phrase “and if he will not redeem the field” is referring to a case where the owner did not redeem it and it remained in the possession of the Temple treasury, and the phrase “or if he sold the field” is referring to a situation where the Temple treasurer sold it to another person. The verse indicates that in both of these instances, possession of the field goes to the priests.

notes.dh: ואם מכר את השדה גזבר לאיש אחר לא יגאל עוד
notes.he: לבעלים אלא חוזר לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: “And if he sold the field”: the treasurer, “to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore” by the owner, but it returns to the priests in the Jubilee.

messages.text: “To another man,” indicates that the field is transferred to the priests during the Jubilee Year only if it had been sold to another, and not to the son of the one who consecrated it.

notes.he: והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל לכהנים:
notes.en: Gemara. To another man: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” [shall be] for the priests.

notes.he: שאם גאלה בנו אינה יוצאה לכהנים אלא לאביו:
notes.en: And not to the son: for if his son redeemed it, it does not go out to the priests but to his father.

notes.he: שאם מכרה גיזבר לבן המקדיש חוזרת לאביו ביובל:
notes.en: To another and not to the son: for if the treasurer sold it to the son of the one who consecrated it, it returns to his father in the Jubilee.

messages.text: Do you say that the verse is referring to another and not to his son? Or perhaps the verse means only that it was sold to another and not to his brother?
When it says: “Man,” the brother is stated, i.e., he is included in the category of a man. How do I realize the meaning of: “Another man”? It must mean: Another, but not his son.

notes.he: שיהא כאחר ותצא לכהנים:
notes.en: The brother is stated: that he is like another, and it goes out to the priests.

notes.he: סתם משמע אחיו דלא יגאל עוד:
notes.en: When it says “man”: unqualified, it implies his brother, [so that] it shall not be redeemed anymore.

notes.he: לאחר לא יגאל ולא לבן:
notes.en: Why must the verse state “another”? To another it shall not be redeemed, but not to the son.

messages.text: And what did you see to include the son in the same category as the father, and to exclude the brother?

I include the son, as he stands in place of his father with regard to designating a Hebrew maidservant as a wife for himself, in a case where the father purchased the Hebrew maidservant and designates her as a wife for his son, which he cannot do for his brother. And he also stands in place of his father with regard to a Hebrew slave, as when one inherits a Hebrew slave from his father, the slave is obligated to serve the son and does not go free, whereas if the deceased’s brother inherits the servant, he goes free.

notes.he: שאם קנה אביו אמה העבריה ורוצה בה ליעדה לו מיעדה ואין צריך לקדשה בכסף אחר אלא באותו כסף שנתן בה אביו כשקנאה היא מקודשת לו כדמפרש בפ"ק דקדושין (דף יט:):
notes.en: For designation: if his father bought a Hebrew maidservant and he [the son] wants to designate her for himself, he designates her; he need not betroth her with other money, but with that same money his father gave for her when he bought her she is betrothed to him, as is explained in the first chapter of Kiddushin (19b).

notes.he: דעובד את הבן אם מת אדוניו בתוך ו' שנים ואינו עובד את האח אם מת אדוניו בלא בן ואחיו יורשו אין זה עובדו כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף יז:) ה"נ מוקמינן בן במקום אב לשדה אחוזה דכי היכי דאינה יוצאה מיד אביו להתחלק לכהנים אם גאלו בנו לא תצא לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: And for a Hebrew slave: he serves the son if his master died within the six years, but he does not serve the brother: if his master died without a son and his brother inherits him, he does not serve him, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (17b). So too we set the son in place of the father for an ancestral field: just as it does not leave his father’s possession to be divided among the priests [when the father redeems it], if his son redeemed it, it does not go out to the priests in the Jubilee.

notes.he: וא"ת אמאי לא חשיב נמי לנחלה ואין לומר דמשום דלא ידעינן נחלה אלא מטעם זה שהוא קודם לשדה אחוזה כדאיתא בפרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קח:) הא ליתא דאפילו יהא שוים בשאר דברים כמו עבד עברי ושדה אחוזה מכל מקום ליעידה הבן קודם לאח בקרא בהדיא ומיניה ידעינן שפיר נחלה לכן נראה לפרש דלא נקט אלא דלא שייכא באח כלל אבל נחלה שייכא באח מיהא היכא דליכא לא בן ולא בת (ולא אב):
notes.en: (Belongs to amud b.) For designation and for a Hebrew slave: And if you say: why does it not also count inheritance? One cannot say it is because we know [the son’s precedence in] inheritance only by this reasoning, that he precedes for an ancestral field, as is found in the chapter Yesh Noḥalin (Bava Batra 108b). That is not so, for even if they were equal in other matters, such as a Hebrew slave and an ancestral field, in any case for designation the son precedes the brother explicitly in the verse, and from it we know inheritance well. Therefore it seems right to explain that it mentions only matters that do not apply to a brother at all; but inheritance does apply to a brother, at least where there is neither son nor daughter (nor father).

notes.he: דכתיב אם לבנו יעדנה:
notes.en: [For designation: as it is written: “And if he designates her for his son” (Exodus 21:9).

messages.text: On the contrary, I should include the brother, as he stands in his brother’s place with regard to levirate marriage, which a son does not.

Is there ever a case of levirate marriage other than a case where there is no son? In a case where there is a son there is no levirate marriage. This indicates that with regard to levirate marriage as well, a son stands in place of the deceased more than a brother of the deceased.

notes.dh: כלום יש יבום אלא במקום שאין בן
notes.he: פי' ועדיף טפי בן מאח בהאי מילתא אבל אין לפרש כדמשמע לפום ריהטא דשוים הם בדבר הזה והוה ליה בן עדיף ביעידה ועבד עברי דלא משמע כך ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קט.) דמסיק דבת קודמת לאב ולאח מטעם זה דלענין יבום בן ובת כי הדדי נינהו לענין נחלה נמי בן ובת כי הדדי נינהו אלמא ע"כ אנו צריכין לומר דמטעם זה בן עדיף טפי מאח:
notes.en: Is there ever levirate marriage other than where there is no son? Meaning: and the son is preferable to the brother in this matter. But one should not explain, as it appears at first glance, that they are equal in this matter and so the son is preferable through designation and the Hebrew slave. For that is not how it appears in Yesh Noḥalin (Bava Batra 109a), which concludes that a daughter precedes the father and the brother for this very reason: with regard to levirate marriage a son and a daughter are alike, so with regard to inheritance too a son and a daughter are alike. Evidently we must say that for this reason the son is preferable to the brother.

messages.text: Why is it necessary to answer the question in this way? Let one derive the halakha that the son stands in place of the father, and the brother does not, from the simple fact that here, in support of extending the father’s status to the son, there are two justifications, i.e., the halakha of designation of the Hebrew maidservant and the halakha of the Hebrew slave, and there, in support of extending it to the brother, there is only one justification, i.e., the halakha of levirate marriage?
messages.quote: designating … with regard to a Hebrew slave

notes.he: ול"ל לתרוצי כלום יש יבום כו':
notes.en: And let him derive it from the fact that here there are two, and so on: and he would not need to answer: Is there ever levirate marriage, and so on.

messages.text: That answer is invalid because the halakha that a son, but not a brother, stands in place of his father with regard to a Hebrew slave is not written explicitly in the Torah, but the tanna also derives it from this same refutation, namely: Is there ever a case of levirate marriage other than a case where there is no son. Without this refutation there would not be more justifications in support of extending the father’s status to the son rather than to the brother. Accordingly, this last refutation is the basis for the conclusion.
messages.quote: Is there ever a case of levirate marriage other than a case where there is no son?

notes.he: דהא דבן קם תחת אביו לעבד עברי לא נפקא לן מקרא אלא מהאי פירכא דכלום יש יבום וכו' דאמרי' בקדושין (דף יז:) מה ראית לרבות את הבן לעבד עברי ולהוציא את האח מרבה אני את הבן שכן קם תחת אביו ליעידה אדרבה מרבה אני את האח שכן קם תחת אחיו ליבום ומשני כלום יש יבום אלא במקום שאין בן ואי לאו האי פירכא דכלום יש יבום כו' לא נפקא ליה בעבד עברי והוה ליה הכא חדא והכא חדא:
notes.en: Because: that the son stands in place of his father for a Hebrew slave is derived for us not from a verse but from this refutation, “Is there ever levirate marriage,” and so on, as we say in Kiddushin (17b): What did you see to include the son for a Hebrew slave and to exclude the brother? I include the son, as he stands in place of his father for designation. On the contrary, I include the brother, as he stands in place of his brother for levirate marriage. And it answers: Is there ever levirate marriage other than where there is no son? And were it not for this refutation, “Is there ever levirate marriage,” and so on, he would not have derived it for a Hebrew slave, and it would be one here and one there.

notes.he: והכא יבום לחודיה משום הכי לא פריך הא והכא תרתי משום דעבד עברי מהאי פירכא כלום יש כו' הוא דנפקא הוא דאיתרבי דהכי גמרינן במסכת קדושין דעבד עברי עובד את הבן ולא את האח אתה אומר את הבן או אינו אלא האח ולא את הבן מרבה אני את הבן שקם תחת אביו ליעידה ולשדה אחוזה אדרבה מרבה אני את האח שקם תחת (אביו) [אחיו] ליבום. ופרכינן אההוא אדרבה ואמרינן כלום יש יבום אלא במקום שאין בן הא יש בן אין יבום ומהתם איתרבה עבד עברי דהבן קם תחת אביו לעבד עברי דלא אשכחן ליה קרא אלא ליעידה גרידה אשכחן קרא שקם תחתיו הילכך ליכא לפרוכי ותיפוק לי דהתם תרתי דלא אשכחן לתרוייהו מקרא אלא האי פרכינן כלום יש יבום במקום בן והוה ליה כחדא וחדא:
notes.en: [A printer’s note: it seems it should read: Because of the Hebrew slave; that is why it does not object “here there are two and here levirate marriage alone,” because the Hebrew slave, and so on.] And for a Hebrew slave; and here, levirate marriage alone. That is why it does not object “here there are two,” because the Hebrew slave is derived from this refutation, “Is there ever,” and so on; it is from there that it is included. For so we learn in tractate Kiddushin: a Hebrew slave serves the son and not the brother. Do you say the son, or perhaps the brother and not the son? I include the son, who stands in place of his father for designation and for an ancestral field. On the contrary, I include the brother, who stands in place of (his father) [his brother] for levirate marriage. And we refute that “on the contrary” and say: Is there ever levirate marriage other than where there is no son? So where there is a son there is no levirate marriage. And from there the Hebrew slave is included, that the son stands in place of his father for a Hebrew slave; for we found a verse that he stands in his place only for designation alone. Therefore one cannot object “let him derive it from the fact that there it is two,” since we did not find a verse for both, only this refutation, “Is there levirate marriage where there is a son,” and it is like one against one.

messages.text: If a daughter redeemed the ancestral field that her father consecrated, what is the halakha? Does she thereby preserve possession of the field for her father at the Jubilee Year, like a son?

notes.he: אם גאלתה בתו לשדה אחוזה מיד גזבר מהו שיצא לאביה ביובל ולא לכהנים:
notes.en: What is the halakha with regard to whether she preserves, and so on: if his daughter redeemed an ancestral field from the treasurer, what is the halakha with regard to whether it goes out to her father in the Jubilee and not to the priests?

notes.he: כלומר אם גאלה בתו מהו שתעמוד שדה לאביה שתחזור לו ביובל]:
notes.en: A daughter, what is the halakha with regard to whether she preserves: that is, if his daughter redeemed it, what is the halakha with regard to whether she preserves the field for her father, so that it returns to him in the Jubilee?]

messages.text: Perhaps the halakha is that since with regard to levirate marriage, a son and a daughter are like one another, as both exempt their father’s widow from the obligation of levirate marriage, the daughter preserves possession of the field for her father. Or perhaps the halakha is that since with regard to inheritance, when there is a son, a daughter is considered like another person, as she does not inherit a share of her father’s estate, she does not preserve possession of the field for her father.
Come and hear a proof from a baraita that the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
messages.quote: a daughter … preserve possession of the field for her father

messages.text: Anyone who is considered like another person when there is a son does not preserve possession of the field for the owner.

notes.he: דהיכא דיש בן חשוב זה כאחר אינו מעמיד:
notes.en: Anyone who is another in the place of a son: where there is a son, this one is considered like another and does not preserve it.

messages.text: And with regard to this, i.e., a daughter, as well, when there is a son, she is considered like another person.

notes.dh: כיון דבת במקום בן כי אחר דמיא
notes.he: הכי נמי דכי הויא שלא במקום בן נמי לא מוקמה [שדה] לאביה:
notes.en: Since a daughter in the place of a son is like another: so too when she is not in the place of a son, she does not preserve the [field] for her father.

messages.text: If a woman consecrated her ancestral field, which of her heirs can redeem the field and thereby preserve possession of the field for her during the Jubilee Year?

notes.he: שהקדישה שדה מלוג מי יפדנה מיד הקדש שלא תצא לכהנים ביובל אם היא אינה יכולה לפדותה:
notes.en: A woman: who consecrated a field of her usufruct property [milog]: who may redeem it from the Temple so that it does not go out to the priests in the Jubilee, if she herself cannot redeem it?

notes.he: (אשה שהקדישה שדה מכר לה [הגזבר] וגאלה בעלה מי יעמוד לה בעלה שדה שתהא שלה ביובל מי חשבינן כאילו היא עצמה גאלתו):
notes.en: (A woman who consecrated a field, [the treasurer] sold it to her [sic], and her husband redeemed it: does her husband preserve the field for her, so that it is hers in the Jubilee? Do we consider it as though she herself redeemed it?)

notes.he: [אשה שהקדישה שדה מלוג שלה וגאלה בעלה מי מעמיד לה בעלה שדה שתהא שלה ביובל מי חשבינן כאילו היא עצמה גאלתו]:
notes.en: [A woman who consecrated her usufruct field and her husband redeemed it: does her husband preserve the field for her, so that it is hers in the Jubilee? Do we consider it as though she herself redeemed it?]

messages.text: Can her husband preserve it for her, as he inherits from her if she dies during his lifetime? Or perhaps her son can preserve it for her, as if the son inherits from his mother, when she was not married at the time of her death, he takes in inheritance the property due to her as he does the property she possessed?

notes.he: דהוא ירית לה אפי' יש לה בן בעלה יורשה ולא בן כדכתיב וירש אותה מלמד שהבעל יורש את אשתו (ב"ב דף קיא:):
notes.en: As he inherits her: for he inherits her even if she has a son; her husband inherits her and not the son, as it is written: “and he shall inherit it” [Numbers 27:11], which teaches that the husband inherits his wife (Bava Batra 111b).

notes.he: דהא היכא דאין בעל ובנה יורשה נוטל בנכסים הראוים ליפול לאחר מיתה כבמוחזק לה לפני מיתה אבל בעל היורש את אשתו אינו נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק כדאמרינן בפרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קיג.):
notes.en: Or perhaps the son preserves it for her: for where there is no husband and her son inherits her, he takes property due to fall to her after death as he does property held before death; but a husband who inherits his wife does not take what is due as he does what is held, as we say in the chapter Yesh Noḥalin (Bava Batra 113a).

notes.he: שכן הבן נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק כדמפרש ביש נוחלין ויפה כח הבן מכח האב:
notes.en: As the son takes what is due as what is held, as is explained in Yesh Noḥalin; and the son’s power is greater than the father’s.

messages.text: There is a halakha that if someone dies and his heir is a woman who is already deceased, her son inherits that property, not her late husband. No resolution is offered, and therefore the dilemma shall stand unresolved.

If one consecrated his ancestral field less than two years before the Jubilee Year and did not redeem it, what is the halakha with regard to whether or not it is to be removed from his possession during the Jubilee and given to the priests?
messages.lead: § Rami bar Ḥama raised a dilemma before Rav Ḥisda:

notes.dh: הקדישה פחות משתי שנים לפני היובל
notes.he: ובא אחר וגאלה ולא בגירוע אלא חמשים שלימין מהו שתצא לכהנים ביובל כשאר שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: He consecrated it less than two years before the Jubilee: and another came and redeemed it, not with a deduction but for a full fifty. What is the halakha with regard to whether it goes out to the priests in the Jubilee like any ancestral field? [Rashi reads the case as one where another person redeemed the field; the Davidson English speaks of a field that was not redeemed.]

messages.text: What is your reasoning? Is it that since the verse states: “And a deduction shall be made from your valuation,” which indicates that the field is redeemed with a deduction according to the years remaining until the Jubilee Year, and the verse also states: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord…his ancestral possession shall be for the priest,” this indicates that if the field is fit for deduction, then yes, when it is not redeemed by the owner it is given to the priests at the Jubilee Year, but with regard to a field that is not fit for deduction, i.e., one consecrated less than two years before the Jubilee Year, which must be redeemed according to its full valuation (24a), no, it is not given to the priests but rather is returned to the owner?
messages.quote: less than two years before the Jubilee

verse.he: וְאִם־אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף עַל־פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verse.en: But if the land is consecrated after the jubilee, the priest shall compute the price according to the years that are left until the jubilee year, and its assessment shall be so reduced;

notes.he: דתיבעי למימר דלא נפקא:
notes.en: What is your reasoning: that you would want to say it does not go out.

notes.he: [דלאו בת גירעון לא יוצא לכהנים דפחות מב' שנים אינו מגרע אלא נותן נ' שקל]:
notes.en: [For one that is not fit for deduction does not go out to the priests, since for less than two years one does not deduct but gives fifty shekels.]

messages.text: On the contrary, the verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore. But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord…his ancestral possession shall be for the priest.” This indicates that any field that could have been redeemed but was not redeemed becomes the possession of the priests. And this field, which was consecrated less than two years before the Jubilee Year, is also fit for redemption. Therefore, if it was not redeemed it is given to the priests.

verse.he: וְאִם־לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה וְאִם־מָכַר אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד׃ וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: But if the one [who consecrated it] did not redeem the land, and the land was sold to another party, it shall no longer be redeemable: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: [ואם לא גאלה] תצא לכהנים:
notes.en: And this too is fit for redemption: [and if he did not redeem it,] it goes out to the priests.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: If one of the priests redeemed the field and when the Jubilee Year arrived it was in his possession, he may not say: Since it is removed from the possession of the one who redeemed it and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, and since it is already in my possession, it is mine. Rather, the field is removed from his possession and is divided among all of his brethren, the priests.
messages.quote: If one of the priests redeemed the field

messages.text: Why must the verse state: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord…his ancestral possession shall be for the priest”?
messages.lead: With regard to this halakha, the Sages taught in a baraita:

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: [ליכתוב] לכהן תהיה:
notes.en: “His ancestral possession”, why must the verse state it? [It could have written:] “shall be for the priest.”

messages.text: From where is it derived, with regard to a field that was consecrated and not redeemed by the owner, and therefore was to have been removed from the possession of the owner and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, and one of the priests redeemed it before the Jubilee, from where is it derived that he may not say: Since it is removed from the possession of the owner and given to the priest at the Jubilee, and since it is already in my possession, it should therefore be mine?

notes.he: שראוי לתת לכהנים ביובל שהקדישה בעלים ולא גאלה:
notes.en: With regard to a field that goes out to the priests: one fit to be given to the priests in the Jubilee, which the owner consecrated and did not redeem.

notes.he: מיד גזבר:
notes.en: And one of the priests redeemed it: from the treasurer.

notes.he: שלא גאלוה בעלים ולא בנו אלא כהן או אחר שהיא יוצאה לכהנים ביובל מנין שלא יאמר כו':
notes.en: With regard to a field that goes out to the priests: one that neither the owner nor his son redeemed, but a priest or another, so that it goes out to the priests in the Jubilee: from where do we know that he may not say, and so on.

messages.text: And this claim is supported by a logical inference: Since in the Jubilee Year I obtain fields of others that I did not previously redeem, is it not all the more so clear that I should retain my own field that I redeemed from the Temple treasury myself?

notes.he: אם גאלה ישראל היתה יוצאה מידו ואני זוכה בה עם שאר אחיי:
notes.en: I acquire [fields] of others: had an Israelite redeemed it, it would go out of his possession and I would acquire it with the rest of my brethren.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “His ancestral possession,” which can be interpreted to mean that only his ancestral field, i.e., one that the priest inherited from his own ancestors, is automatically his, but this field is not his. How so, i.e., how is this field treated? It is removed from his possession and is divided among all of his brethren, the priests.

notes.he: ואיכא למידרש הכי אחוזתו של כהן שירש מאביו תהא שלו אבל זו אינה שלו:
notes.en: The verse states: “His ancestral possession shall be for the priest”: it can be expounded thus: the ancestral possession of a priest, which he inherited from his father, shall be his; but this one is not his.

notes.he: וא"ת ל"ל אחוזתו בלא קרא נוכל לסתור הק"ו כדאיתא בסוף מכילתין גבי שדה חרמין דדייק ק"ו כה"ג דהכא ומסיק מי דמי התם קא זכי בעלמא הכא שקיל ליה ה"נ הוה מצי למסתר ק"ו וי"ל דאי לאו אחוזתו ה"א מג"ש דכהן כהן מגזל הגר דאינה יוצאה מתחת ידו וכן משמע הסוגיא התם פרק הגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף קט: ושם) דת"ר הרי שהיה כהן גוזל הגר מנין שלא יאמר הואיל ויוצא לכהנים והרי הוא תחת ידי תהא שלי ודין הוא אם בשל אחרים זוכה בשל עצמו לא כ"ש [וכו'] והכתיב איש את קדשיו לו יהיה פירוש דמיניה ילפינן (שם) דכהן מקריב קרבנותיו בכל עת ובכל שעה שירצה ואפי' במשמר שאינו שלו וא"כ דין הוא שיקריב אשמו שהוא חייב על גזל הגר וישאר גם הקרן בידו [ומשני] דילפינן כהן כהן משדה אחוזה דיוצא מתחת ידו ומתחלקת לכל [אחיו] הכהנים והתם מנלן ומייתי סוגיא דהכא אלמא אי לא דכתיב אחוזתו ה"א בגזל הגר דאינו יוצא מתחת ידו משום דכתיב ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיה וילפינן נמי שדה שהיא אחוזה דאינה יוצאה מיד כהן מש"ה איצטריך אחוזתו שלו ואין זו שלו וילפינן גזל הגר מיניה מג"ש דכהן כהן:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot ask why the word “his ancestral possession” is needed at all, since the a fortiori argument could be refuted without a verse, as at the end of this tractate regarding a field of dedications, where a similar a fortiori is rejected: there the priest merely acquires in general, here he takes it [into his own hands]. They answer that without “his ancestral possession” one would have derived, by the verbal analogy “priest”–“priest” from property stolen from a convert, that the field does not leave the priest’s possession. So the passage in Bava Kamma (109b) shows: a baraita asks, where a priest robbed a convert [who died without heirs], from where do we know that he may not say: since it goes out to the priests and it is in my possession, let it be mine? It is logical: if I acquire what is others’, all the more so what is mine. And it is written: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his” [Numbers 5:10], from which it is derived that a priest may offer his own offerings whenever he wishes, even in a watch not his own; so he should offer his guilt offering for robbing the convert and keep the principal as well. The Gemara there answers that we derive “priest”–“priest” from an ancestral field, which goes out of his possession and is divided among all his brethren the priests, and to show the source for that it cites this passage. Evidently, were it not for “his ancestral possession,” one would have said that the convert’s stolen property does not leave the priest’s possession because of “every man’s hallowed things shall be his,” and one would have derived that the ancestral field too does not leave the priest’s possession. That is why “his ancestral possession: it is his, and this is not his” is needed, and the convert’s stolen property is derived from it by the verbal analogy “priest”–“priest.” Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: של עצמו היא שלו:
notes.en: “His ancestral possession”: his own is his.

notes.he: לבדו הא כיצד כו':
notes.en: And this is not his: alone. How so, and so on.

messages.text: Mishna
If one consecrated his ancestral field and the Jubilee Year arrived and it was not redeemed by the owner or anyone else:
The priests enter into the field and give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: כהנים של משמר היובל נכנסין לתוכה כו' והיא חלוטה בידם:
notes.en: Mishna. The priests enter into it, and so on: the priests of the [priestly] watch [serving] at the Jubilee enter into it, and so on, and it is permanently theirs.

notes.he: דכתיב לכהן תהיה:
notes.en: The priests enter into it: as it is written: “shall be for the priest.”

notes.he: להקדש דכתיב קדש לה':
notes.en: And give its value: to the Temple, as it is written: “holy to the Lord.”

messages.text: They enter into the field, but they do not give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury.

The priests do not enter into the field, and they also do not give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury. Rather, the field remains in the possession of the Temple treasury, and it is called: An abandoned field, until the second Jubilee Year.

notes.he: עזובה עד שיגאלנה אחר וכשיגיע יובל תצא מידו לכהנים:
notes.en: An abandoned field: left alone until another redeems it, and when the Jubilee arrives it goes out of his possession to the priests.

notes.he: שדה מונחת שאין רשות לאדם בה כדכתיב תשמטנה ונטשתה ומתרגמינן ותרטשנה [עד יובל שני]:
notes.en: Rather, it is called an abandoned field: a field left lying, in which no one has any right, as it is written: “you shall let it rest and lie fallow [unetashtah]” [Exodus 23:11], which the Aramaic translation renders “and leave it abandoned [vetirteshinah]”, [until the second Jubilee].

messages.text: If the second Jubilee arrived and it was still not redeemed, it is called: An abandoned field from among the abandoned fields, meaning one that was abandoned twice, until the third Jubilee. In any case, the priests never enter into a consecrated field during the Jubilee Year until another person redeems it first.

notes.he: שלא יגע אדם בה עד יובל ג' שלעולם אין הכהנים נכנסין לתוכה עד שיגאלנה אחר מיד הגזבר כדכתיב ואם מכר את השדה. גיזבר לאיש אחר לא יגאל עוד לבעלים אלא והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל:
notes.en: Abandoned of the abandoned: no one may touch it until the third Jubilee, for the priests never enter into it until another redeems it from the treasurer, as it is written: “or if he sold the field” (the treasurer) “to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore” by the owner, but “the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” [shall be for the priest].

messages.text: Gemara
What is the reason for Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion that the priests who enter into an unredeemed consecrated field during the Jubilee Year must give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury?
messages.quote: The priests enter into the field and give its redemption payment

notes.he: דקאמר הכא ונותן את דמיה:
notes.en: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda: who says here “and they give its value.”

messages.text: He derives this halakha from a verbal analogy from the word “holy” stated in reference to an ancestral field, and the word “holy” that appears with regard to one who consecrates a house.

notes.he: במקדיש בית כתיב כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש ובשדה אחוזה כתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י״ד) בצאתו ביובל קודש וגו' מה בית לא תצא לעולם מיד הקדש בלא דמים כדכתיב התם והעריכו הכהן וגו' ובית לא נפקא לכהנים לעולם אלא שדה אחוזה לחודה דגזירת מלך היא אף שדה אחוזה לא תצא מיד הקדש בלא דמים הילכך כי פריק לה אחר הרי דמיה לבדק הבית הקדש וכי מטי יובל נפקא בחנם לכהנים ואי לא נגאלה יהבי כהנים דמי חמשים שקל ושקלי לה:
notes.en: Gemara. From one who consecrates a house: regarding one who consecrates a house it is written (Leviticus 27:14): “When a man shall sanctify his house to be holy,” and regarding an ancestral field it is written: “when it goes out in the Jubilee, holy,” and so on [Leviticus 27:21]. Just as a house never leaves the Temple’s possession without money, as it is written there: “Then the priest shall value it,” and so on (and a house never goes out to the priests; only an ancestral field does, for it is a royal decree), so too an ancestral field does not leave the Temple’s possession without money. Therefore, when another redeems it, its money has gone to Temple maintenance, and when the Jubilee arrives it goes out to the priests for free; and if it was not redeemed, the priests give its money, fifty shekels, and take it.

messages.text: Just as there, with regard to one who consecrates a house, where the verse states: “And when a man shall consecrate his house to be holy for the Lord,” it can be redeemed from the Temple treasury only by payment of money, as the verse concludes: “As the priest shall value it, so shall it stand,” so too here, where the verse states with regard to the priests entering into an ancestral field: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord…his ancestral possession shall be for the priest” (Leviticus 27:21), the priests can enter the field only by payment of money.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יַקְדִּשׁ אֶת־בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יָקוּם׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who consecrates a house to GOD: The priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, as the priest assesses it, so it shall stand;

notes.dh: מה להלן בדמים אף כאן בדמים
notes.he: וא"ת מנלן דיש להן לכהנים עליה טפי מאחר דלמא דומיא דמקדיש בית דיוצא בדמים לכל מי שירצה וכהן וישראל שוין בו ה"נ הוה לן למימר בזה וי"ל דמשמע ליה פשטיה דקרא הכי ואם לא יגאל את השדה פי' הבעלים אלא עומד ביד הגזבר עד יובל ואם מכר השדה לאיש אחר שגאלו אחר בשני דרכים אלו לא יגאל עוד הבעלים מיד הקדש אלא והיה בצאתו ביובל קדש לה' לכהנים יהיה אלמא משמע מתוך הפסוקים שיוצא ליד כהנים ואתיא ג"ש לר' יהודה לאשמועינן שיוצא בדמים ולא בחנם היכא דלא גאלה אחר:
notes.en: Just as there it is by money, so too here by money: And if you say: from where do we know that the priests have more claim to it than another? Perhaps it is like one who consecrates a house, which goes out for money to whoever wishes, priest and Israelite alike; so too we should say here. One can say that the plain meaning of the verse implies it to him: “And if he will not redeem the field,” meaning the owner, but it stands in the treasurer’s possession until the Jubilee; “or if he sold the field to another man,” meaning another redeemed it: in these two ways the owner shall not redeem it again from the Temple, but rather “the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy to the Lord … for the priest.” Evidently the verses imply that it goes out into the priests’ possession, and the verbal analogy comes, for Rabbi Yehuda, to teach that it goes out for money and not for free, where another did not redeem it.

notes.he: [כתיב הכא קדש לה' כשדה החרם וכתיב ואיש כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש] מה להלן [בבית] בדמים דכתיב ויסף חמישית כסף [אף כאן בדמים:
notes.en: [It is written here: “holy to the Lord, as a dedicated field,” and it is written: “And when a man shall sanctify his house to be holy.”] Just as there [with a house] it is by money, as it is written: “he shall add the fifth part of the money” [Leviticus 27:15], [so too here by money.

messages.text: And what is the source for the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who maintains that the priests are not required to give the redemption payment to the Temple treasury?
messages.quote: but they do not give its redemption payment

notes.he: תימה שהרי בתחילה שואל הספר מ"ט דר' יהודה אלמא טעמא דר"ש מסתבר טפי בלא ג"ש ואח"כ שואל מה טעם דר' שמעון אלמא דרבי יהודה מסתבר טפי וי"ל דאשכחן נמי כי האי גוונא בבא קמא (דף י:) גבי הכוהו עשרה בני אדם בעשר מקלות דלמר משמע כי יכה כל נפש עד שיכה כל נפש ולמר משמע כל דהו נפש ונ"ל דלפי מה דפירשתי ניחא דפשטיה דקרא משתמע שיצא לכהנים ולא איצטריך גזירה שוה לומר דיוצא בדמים ולמר אצטריך גזרה שוה דיוצא בחנם:
notes.en: And Rabbi Shimon, what is the reason? This is puzzling: at first the Gemara asks what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda, implying that Rabbi Shimon’s view is more plausible without a verbal analogy, and afterward it asks what is the reason of Rabbi Shimon, implying that Rabbi Yehuda’s is more plausible. One can say that we find the like in Bava Kamma (10b), regarding ten people who struck a man with ten sticks: to one Sage [the verse] “when he strikes any soul” implies until he strikes the whole soul, and to the other it implies any bit of soul. And it seems to me that according to what I explained it is well: the plain meaning of the verse implies that it goes out to the priests, and no verbal analogy would be needed to say that it goes out for money; and for the other Sage a verbal analogy is needed [to teach] that it goes out for free.

messages.text: He derives the halakha from the word “holy” used with regard to an ancestral field, and the word “holy” used with regard to the communal peace offering of two lambs that accompanies the two loaves on Shavuot. Just as there, with regard to the offering of two lambs, where the verse states: “They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest,” the lambs are given to the priests for free, as is the halakha with regard to all offerings to which members of the priesthood are entitled, so too here, the consecrated and unredeemed ancestral field is given to the priests for free.

verse.he: וְהֵנִיף הַכֹּהֵן ׀ אֹתָם עַל לֶחֶם הַבִּכֻּרִים תְּנוּפָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה עַל־שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׂים קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיוּ לַיהֹוָה לַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: The priest shall elevate these—the two lambs—together with the bread of first fruits as an elevation offering before GOD; they shall be holy to GOD, for the priest.

notes.he: בכבשי עצרת כתיב (ויקרא כ״ג:כ׳-כ״א) קודש יהיו לה' לכהן: כבשי עצרת ושדה אחוזה מכ"ד מתנות כהונה נינהו (במדבר יח) אבל בית לא הויא לעולם לכהנים ואפי' גאלה אחר מיד הקדש:
notes.en: Regarding the lambs of Shavuot it is written (Leviticus 23:20–21): “They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest.” The lambs of Shavuot and the ancestral field are among the twenty-four gifts of the priesthood (Numbers 18), but a house never belongs to the priests, even if another redeemed it from the Temple.

notes.he: דכתיב בהן קדש יהיה לה' לכהן בחנם]:
notes.en: From the lambs of Shavuot: of which it is written: “They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest,” for free.]

messages.caption: The Jubilee arrives and no one has redeemed the field: the mishna’s three opinions, and the verbal analogies the Gemara gives for Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Yehuda, let him also derive the halakha by a verbal analogy from the two lambs brought on Shavuot. Why does he disagree with Rabbi Shimon?
One derives the halakha with regard to items consecrated for Temple maintenance, such as an ancestral field,

notes.he: דבין בית ובין דמי שדה אחוזה הוו קדשי בדק הבית:
notes.en: One derives items consecrated for Temple maintenance, and so on: for both a house and the value of an ancestral field are items consecrated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: שדה אחוזה וכבשי עצרת הוו מתנה לכהנים דבתרווייהו כתיב לכהן יהיה ולא במקדיש בית:
notes.en: An ancestral field and the lambs of Shavuot are a gift to the priests, for of both it is written “shall be for the priest,” but not of one who consecrates a house. [This note explains the Gemara’s next answer, on 26a.]

messages.text: Continues on 26a: … from other items consecrated for Temple maintenance, such as a consecrated house, but not from items consecrated for the altar, such as the lambs of Shavuot. The Gemara then asks why Rabbi Shimon does not learn from the house.
